title: The Apollo engagement: long solos by Dizzy and Dexter
summary: The hip New York audience loves Sarah and the soloists, who stretch out for many choruses, unlike earlier big bands.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: We opened in the Apollo Theatre with a very successful engagement, and it turned out to be one of our best... You know, we were most right there, simply because New York is... You know, the hipness of the New York audience, and they really loved Sarah, they loved the soloists... It was the only theatre I remember playing with any band, except maybe some small groups, but even the small groups, the soloists played as many choruses as they wanted... Because in those days, you played a show, which usually the show was about an hour-and-a-half... You played the show a certain length of time, I guess, probably somewhere about a 45-50 minute show, and then the band took over and did their bit. The band was always the main attraction. At times I've seen Dizzy and Dexter Gordon start up on the stage and play, like, six, seven and eight choruses on a tune, which is something that most big bands before that didn't have anything like that at all, except for maybe a band like Basie, where a guy would play a couple of

choruses or something -- but they never really had things that stretched out like that. . And in the Apollo Theatre, the audience just loved it, you know, because Dizzy was young and strong then, and Dexter was the same... Dexter was about 21 then -- 21 or 22. Then, to me, he was playing a different style than what he does now. It was similar, but I think he's playing much more commercially now than he was then. He always was a good player, in my estimation, and still is...

But after that, we had this stamp on us, and I guess the rest of it is pretty much history as far as the band is concerned. The only bad thing about it was that it was at the wrong time. It was during the War, and this particular time that I'm talking about was in September of 1944. It could have been October. But it was in the Fall of 1944. I remember that the weather was still warm and everything.
